name: Project Open Hand
description: Project Open Hand provides medically tailored meals and groceries to people living with serious illnesses in San Francisco and Alameda County, plus community lunches for older adults and adults with disabilities in San Francisco.
fullDescription: Project Open Hand provides medically tailored meals and groceries to people living with serious illnesses in San Francisco and Alameda County, plus community lunches for older adults and adults with disabilities in San Francisco.
whatTheyOffer:
- Wellness Program - medically tailored meals and groceries for pick-up, with home delivery for homebound clients
- Nutrition counseling from registered dietitians
- Community Nutrition Program - breakfast and lunch at sites across San Francisco for adults 60+ and adults 18-59 with disabilities
- Home-delivered meals for adults with disabilities in San Francisco
- CalAIM Community Supports meals for eligible Medi-Cal members (SF Health Plan, Anthem Blue Cross, Alameda Alliance for Health, Contra Costa Health Plan)
- Two grocery centers
howToGetIt: For the Wellness Program, a licensed medical provider (RN, NP, MD, DO, RD, LCSW, or PA) must complete and sign an application. Eligible diagnoses in San Francisco include HIV/AIDS, COPD, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7%+), end stage renal disease, and recent major surgery; in Alameda County, HIV/AIDS and recent major surgery. CalAIM referrals go through your Medi-Cal health plan. Any San Francisco resident 60+ or 18-59 with a disability can join community meal sites. Call 415-447-2300 (SF) or 510-622-0221 (Oakland).
keywords: Project Open Hand, medically tailored meals, HIV, AIDS, heart failure, COPD, diabetes, kidney disease, surgery recovery, senior meals, CalAIM, Medi-Cal, nutrition counseling, home delivery, Oakland
